title: Brian Eno — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Brian Eno's rich face, its first round, a Sketch and still a proposal: two walks about his method, not his voice. One builds tape loops from a single ring to many and asks whether different lengths are enough to keep a piece from coming round again (not quite: the ratios have to sit far from simple fractions, even to the ear). The other counts the frame choice by choice and puts a coin in the loop, to find where the page's reading of his blind spot holds and where it splits. Every sound is made by the pieces; none of his recordings is here. I grow when the page is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: The sentence is right, just unquantified; the loops piece puts a measure on it. Different lengths drift at a speed set by how near their ratios sit to simple ones: 8, 12, 16 and 24 s never drift (back every 48 s); cut the 24 s loop a sixteenth longer and it drifts slowly, three loops locked at 48 s and the fourth sliding 1/8 s later each cycle (exact return 5.133 h; within 1/8 s once in the first hour, at 48.125 s, on the tolerance's edge). Eno's three (23.5, 25.875, 29.9375 s) come back exactly after 26.97 days and within 1/8 s after 50.6 h, a figure that rests on the precision he quoted ('or something like that'). Near-equal lengths drift too, as Reich's phasing loops do. Numbers confirmed by the challenger in exact fractions. A possible line: '…tape loops of different lengths drifting out of phase: he set the lengths, and how near their ratios sit to simple ones decided how fast it drifts and how soon, if ever, it comes round.'

Scope: in his 1996 talk (In Motion Magazine) Eno describes the loops as 'at least one of the pieces on there'; Wikipedia's article on the record, citing that talk and Tannenbaum 1985, says 2/1 and 1/2 both use vocal loops, while 2/2 (the ARP 2600 piece) is not described as loops. 'Music for Airports is tape loops' slightly overstates; 'the loop pieces on Music for Airports are tape loops of different lengths…' or 'is built mostly from tape loops…' would match both sources. Not checked against the record's credits.

Counted (46.07 questions on the piece's menus, 415 starts an hour, a fair coin 90.0% of the hour, passing the frame at 6.70 min; confirmed by the challenger), the frame piece puts numbers on one half of the blind spot: with ideal loops every start traces back to the frame, which is true of any deterministic machine, so it measures determination, not foresight or taste. A line that keeps the section's tension open rather than settling it: 'With fixed loops every start traces back to the frame; the system adds time, not information. What it adds that he didn't foresee (the chord at 37:12, the wow of the tape, the room) is where the argument starts, not where it ends.'

verdicts.file: Brian Eno — rich — loops of different lengths.html
verdicts.why: A real test that walks up, but the test step shows the nudged set coming round 74 times an hour to the ear when it does so once (floor(3600/te) assumes a steady near-return; the 24.0625 s loop slides 1/8 s a cycle), so its verdict overstates. Count the returns in the hour, say near-simple ratios slow the drift rather than stop it, and use the page's words, "the room made the piece".

pieces.title: loops of different lengths · a walk in four steps
pieces.caption: **He set the lengths. What did the lengths do?** One tape loop alone, then two drifting on a square where one moment is one point, then up to seven, and last a test: are different lengths enough to keep the whole from coming round again? Measured two ways, exactly and to the ear. The notes and the sound are made here; from Eno it takes only three loop lengths he gave in a 1996 talk.

verdicts.why: The counting is right (46.07 questions, 415 starts, 90.0%, 6.70 min), but step 4 is 1533 px in a 1000 px frame, so the verdict is clipped where the kit does not size it, and the verdict closes the page's open question: "decided" should be "determined", and "tape loops have no coin" holds only for ideal loops (the sibling piece names tape's wow, the page credits the room).

pieces.title: the frame, counted · a walk in four steps
pieces.caption: **How much of the drift was chosen?** One chosen loop length, sized in yes/no questions; then the whole frame, tallied; then an hour of loops where any note can be asked who decided it; and last a coin in the loop, Cage's move, to find when the system starts deciding more than the person who framed it.
pieces.near: He chooses the loops, the synths, the constraints, the take
